solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One way to serve meat, keeping it within fine margins

indicators.note: the margins of the next word hold the meat between them, so one piece sits inside the other
the margins of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A chef serves meat while staying within fine tolerances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'margins' of 'fine' gives F and E, and 'keeping it within' puts LAMB between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambéed dish is served doused in spirit and set alight, one method of presenting food.

clue.text: Divine round playground secured by firm

indicators.note: the round and the playground are held fast inside the word for firm

parts.note: firm, as in fixed tight, means fast
O is round in shape
a rec is a recreation ground, British for a public playground

explanation.surface: A firm encloses a playground, the round area perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb here, to foresee or predict; REC (recreation ground) is a British term for a playground or park.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine the future is to predict it, which is what a weather or financial prophecy does.

clue.text: A pink organ towards the rear

parts.note: the Financial Times, a British newspaper (an organ) printed on pink paper

explanation.surface: A pink body part found near the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' means a newspaper here, not a body part; the FT is famous in Britain for its salmon-pink pages.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or aircraft, the stern part is the aft section, toward the back.

clue.text: Singer accepts this country artist's first original idea?

indicators.note: the singer's name takes in the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
GB, Great Britain, the setter's country in a British paper

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word artist's is used

explanation.surface: A singer takes on a British artist's first original idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this country' is GB because the Times is British. The definition is playful: the theory of how the universe began is an idea about origins.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmological theory of the universe's explosive beginning is literally a notion about the origin of everything.

clue.text: After promotion, my French is hard to reproach

indicators.note: the French word comes after the promotion piece in the answer

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
mon is French for my
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone, after being promoted, finds their French hard to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to warn or reprove someone mildly, a synonym for rebuking or reproving.

clue.text: A girl was hunted, possibly becoming one of these?

definitions.text: A girl was hunted, possibly becoming one of these?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the phrase may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A girl who was pursued by a suitor may end up married into his family.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both anagram and definition: a pursued girl who marries the son becomes his parents' relative by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl chased and won by a son becomes, on marrying him, a female relation of his parents by marriage.

clue.text: Old fox maybe grabs Echo, a nymph

indicators.note: the animal word seizes the letter for Echo and holds it inside

parts.note: a fox is an example of a canid, a member of the dog family
Echo is the radio alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: An old fox snatches the nymph Echo.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo is herself a nymph in myth, which tempts a solver to read her as the definition; here she is only the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Oceanids were sea nymphs, daughters of the Titan Oceanus.

clue.text: Distribute no more rings for their suppliers?

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Their vendors are told to hand out no more rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the rings: hardware dealers sell metal rings among nuts, bolts and tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware shops stock metal rings, washers and fittings, so their keepers supply such items.

clue.text: Kind chap put in the shade

indicators.note: the chap is placed inside the colour word

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow is moved into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the shade' is a colour, not shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane people are compassionate and merciful, which is what being kind means.

clue.text: Race soldier to border? Not everyone stands for it

parts.note: the Grand National, Britain's famous steeplechase, is called the National
a soldier ant is a kind of ant
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A race soldier is posted to the border, though not everyone supports him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British horse race. The definition puns: people rise to their feet for the anthem, though some refuse to.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences customarily rise for a country's patriotic song, though some stay seated in protest.

clue.text: Run out to vault containing your print

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: the burial word holds the short form for your within it

parts.note: a burial vault is a grave
ur is a text-speak spelling of your

explanation.surface: Instructions to run out to a vault holding your print.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'run out' when the stumps are hit before he reaches the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotogravure is an intaglio printing process, and a picture produced by it is called by the same name.

clue.text: Hug monarch offering little resistance

parts.note: O stands for a hug, as in the hugs and kisses written XOXO
HM is short for His or Her Majesty, the monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch's hug meets hardly any resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little resistance' is a modest unit of electrical resistance, so 'little' fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, a single one being a small amount.

clue.text: Exactly right to tuck into tea and bread

indicators.note: the precise word is tucked inside the tea word

parts.note: chai is spiced tea, from the Hindi word
off pat means perfectly learned, exactly right

explanation.surface: It's just right to tuck into tea and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' looks like eating but means insertion here.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: A job with strings attached gains Henry marks

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: the cords take in the letter for Henry, which goes inside them

parts.note: ropes are thick strings
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A job with conditions attached earns Henry good grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' suggests conditions, but strings are simply ropes; 'marks' means punctuation, not grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostrophes are punctuation symbols showing omission or possession, so they are written marks.

clue.text: One who used to dispatch game

definitions.meaning: an executioner, who dispatched condemned people before capital punishment ended
a word-guessing pencil game with a gallows drawing

explanation.surface: Someone who once sent off game such as birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Executioners killed by the noose, and the children's guessing game draws one on a gallows.

clue.text: Hunting dogs we'd trained coerced union

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs we had trained were pressed into a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: The shotgun of the answer suits the hunting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage forced on a couple, traditionally because of pregnancy, is a union under coercion.

clue.text: Reply to outburst by Open University bringing in a smaller amount?

indicators.note: the two letters of by take the word for a smaller amount between them

parts.note: taken as written
less is a smaller amount
OU is the Open University, the British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: An outburst at the Open University meets a reply about bringing in less money.
explanation.walkthrough: The outburst is a sneeze, to which the polite reply is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone sneezes, the customary response is this short blessing.

clue.text: Exemplary way with fish knives and forks?

parts.note: stainless means without blemish, morally spotless
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A model way to eat fish, using knives and forks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlery is commonly made of rust-resistant chrome alloy, so the metal can stand for it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Property guardians fill one book actually

indicators.note: the guardians fill a gap between the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic British properties

explanation.surface: Property guardians really do fill one book.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that preserves historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to stress a fact, the phrase means really or in fact, just as actually does.

clue.text: Island's old rules about rudiments of martial arts

indicators.note: the rules wrap around the letters they surround

parts.note: a sutra is an ancient Sanskrit rule or aphorism

indicators.note: rudiments are basics, so only the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: An island's ancient rules surround the basics of martial arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian landmass in the Indian Ocean, west of Java.

clue.text: Cereal covers a large upside-down cake

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down means the letters read from the bottom upward
the cereal goes around the other letters

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Cereal coats a large upside-down cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' reverses RICALE, the rice wrapped around A and L. It looks like it belongs to the upside-down cake of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, a small cake.

clue.text: Gull goes around to crush piece of toast

indicators.note: the trickery word surrounds the defeat word

parts.note: to gull is to dupe, to con
to rout is to crush an enemy

explanation.surface: A seagull circles to crush a bit of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' is the verb to deceive, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread served in soup or salad.

clue.text: Arch rival of Tyneside canteen, I gathered

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: the dining hall word gathers the I into its middle

parts.note: a mess is a military canteen

explanation.surface: A rival of a Tyneside canteen speaks, I gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is a long-standing enemy or opponent, an arch-foe.

clue.text: Spots leader leaving wood

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader of the word, departs

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A spotted leader leaves the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood timber from the tree of that name, used for tool handles.

clue.text: A foreign heath crossed with lily in harmful way

parts.note: un is a or one in French

indicators.note: crossed as in hybridised, so the two plant words are bred together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A foreign heather crossed with a lily is harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed with' mixes HEATH and LILY into HEALTHILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a way bad for one's wellbeing is acting in an injurious or damaging manner.

clue.text: What's crossed by Arctic explorers?

parts.note: polar travellers trek across frozen sea and sheets; the entry also crosses others in the grid

explanation.surface: What do polar explorers traverse?
explanation.definitionFit: The polar regions are covered by frozen water, which expeditions must traverse.

clue.text: Most here not in good shape?

definitions.text: Most here not in good shape?

indicators.note: the letters are out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Most residents here are in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both anagram and definition: most people living in a care home are frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a care home for the elderly are mostly in poor health.

clue.text: Sweet drink invading nearly all of France once

indicators.note: the drink pushes its way into the old country
the old name for France loses its final letter

parts.note: Gaul is the old Roman name for the region of France
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A sweet drink invades almost all of old France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all of' trims GAUL to GAU, which TEA then invades.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cream cake served as a dessert, which British usage calls a sweet.
